passages.t: ‘How good and pleasant it is when brothers live together in harmony’
passages.happening:
Psalm 133 is three verses long. The heading reads, “A song of ascents. Of David” (verse 1). Then: “Behold, how good and pleasant it is when brothers live together in harmony!” (verse 1).

Two pictures follow. Unity “is like fine oil on the head, running down on the beard, running down Aaron's beard over the collar of his robes” (verse 2). “It is like the dew of Hermon falling on the mountains of Zion” (verse 3). And the psalm ends, “For there the LORD has bestowed the blessing of life forevermore” (verse 3).
passages.hearers:
Picture pilgrims from every tribe and village arriving in Jerusalem for a feast. People who might quarrel at home stand side by side. That is one way this psalm has been read: a song of the gathered people of God. The note on Psalm 120 explains the Songs of Ascents. ‘Brothers’ also meant family, and some think the psalm first praised relatives who kept the family land together instead of dividing it.

The oil is the oil Moses poured on Aaron when he was made high priest: “take the anointing oil and anoint him by pouring it on his head” (Exodus 29:7). It ran down and covered him, marking the whole man as set apart for God. Unity is like that: rich, flowing, holy.

Mount Hermon is the high mountain in the far north, known for heavy dew. Zion is far to the south. Dew kept crops alive in the dry months. The picture is of the blessing of the north falling on the south: life-giving moisture where it is needed, shared across the land.

‘There’ in verse 3 means where brothers live in unity, and in Zion, the place of worship. That is where God gives life.
passages.later: Jesus prayed for his followers “that all of them may be one” (John 17:21). The first believers in Jerusalem were “one in heart and soul” (Acts 4:32). Paul urged the church “to preserve the unity of the Spirit through the bond of peace” (Ephesians 4:3).
passages.asks:
Psalm 133 says that unity among God's people is good and also pleasant, a joy and not only a duty. Where is there a quarrel in your family or church that you could help to heal?

Unity in this psalm is not something people make. It runs down from above, like oil and dew. Pray for it as a gift.
